The present Detailed Accidental Report was filed qua the accident dated 15.09.2015.As per the facts of the present case, on 15.09.2015, at about 7.157.30 PM,
on Nangloi Najafgarh Road, in front of Bajrang Enclave, Delhi.
The petitioner was crossing the road, meanwhile a car bearing No. DL 1YD 7728 came from Nangloi side being driven at very fast speed, in rash and negligent manner by R.1, hit the petitioner.
As a result of which he fell down on road and received grievous injuries.
Petitioner sustained multiple fractures of both bones of right leg with left knee and fractured of Pelvic Bone Pubic Rami.
He has suffered 13% permanent physical disability due MACT No. 1646/16 Arun Kumar Vs Ajay Kumar & Ors Page No. 6 of 16 to injuries received in this accident.

After investigation the IO found that said accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing No. DL 1YD 7728 by Ajay Kumar (driver) who has been made respondent no. 1.
S.S Associates Services Pvt Ltd (owner) has been made respondent no. 2 and Future Generali Insurance Company Limited has been made as respondent no. 3.
The present DAR has been filed by the IO.
The DAR has been considered as claim application.
3. The respondents contested the present case.
4. The respondent No.1 has not filed W.S 5.
The respondent No. 2 has filed its W.S stating therein that it was the petitioner/injured who was crossing the road without following the traffic rules and regulations and was hit by unknown car.
It is stated that the car of R.1 was little behind of that unknown car but due to sudden apply of brake the car of R.1 rammed into the rear side of unknown car.

6. The respondent no. 3/Insurance Company has filed its WS and stated that there is violation of terms and condition of Insurance policy as R.1 was driving the offending vehicle without driving license.

7. After competition of pleading, vide an order dated 16.01.2017, the following issues were framed in the present case:
(i) Whether Arun Kumar sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt. 15.09.2015 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle ( Car) No. DL 1YD 7728 being driven by Ajay Kumar , Owned by S.S. Associates Service Pvt Ltd and Insured by R3 Future Generali Insurance Company ?
OPP MACT No. 1646/16 Arun Kumar Vs Ajay Kumar & Ors Page No. 7 of 16 (ii) Whether the petitioner in the above mentioned case is entitled to claim compensation if so, what amount and from whom?

My issue wise findings are as under: ISSUE No. (i): Whether Arun Kumar sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt. 15.09.2015 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle ( Car) No. DL 1YD 7728 being driven by Ajay Kumar , Owned by S.S. Associates Service Pvt Ltd and Insured by R3 Future Generali Insurance Company ?

10.PW 1 in his evidence filed by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A, has deposed that on 15.09.2015, at about 7.157.30 PM, on Nangloi Najafgarh Road, in front of Bajrang Enclave, Delhi, he was crossing the road.
A car bearing No. DL 1YD 7728 came from Nangloi side being driven at very fast speed, in rash and negligent manner by R.1and hit him.
As a result of which he fell down on road and received grievous injuries.
He sustained multiple fractures of both legs of right leg with left knee and fractured of Pelvic Bone Pubic Rami.

He remained admitted in Irena Swastik Hospital,
Najafgarh,Delhi and Lok Nayak Hospital Delhi.

He remained admitted in hospital wef 07.10.2015 to 20.10.2015 and from MACT No. 1646/16 Arun Kumar Vs Ajay Kumar & Ors Page No. 8 of 16 27.10.2015 to 01.11.2015.
11.PW 1 has been crossexamined, but nothing material could come out from his cross examination which could disbelief his testimony.

sentences.text: Being injured, the petitioner was the natural eye witness of the accident.
Even otherwise, the proof of negligence while disposing off a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim was at fault, in any way.
12.The fact that petitioner suffered injuries in that accident is also supported by his medical documents.
After investigation, police also indicted respondent no. 1 as accused for offences punishable under Sections 279/337/338 IPC.
The case has been registered against respondent no. 1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his alleged false implication, if any.
The fact of accident and the respondent no.1 is facing the trial as an accused is not disputed.

Considering all these facts, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of car bearing No. DL 1YD 7728 by respondent no. 1 thereby causing injuries to the petitioner.
ISSUE No.2: ? Whether the petitioner in the above mentioned case is entitled to claim compensation , if so , what amount and from whom? ... OPO 13.

It is there on record, as per the deposition of PW 1 and the MLC annexed with DAR, that he was firstly taken to Irena Swastik Hospital, Najafgarh,Delhi.

Hence , seeing nature of injuries and disability suffered by petitioner, a lump sum amount of Rs. 1,42,800/ is granted to him as compensation towards medical Arun Kumar vs Ajay Kumar on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25153979/

LOSS OF EARNING 15.
It is submitted by Ld Counsel for the Insurance company that there is no evidence qua proving monthly income of the petitioner.
In rebuttal to the submission Ld Counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner is doing Private Job.
However Ld Counsel for the petitioner fairly admitted that he has not placed on record any document qua showing the income of petitioner.
So this Tribunal while assessing the income of injured under Minimum Wages Act prevailing in Delhi has assessed the income of injured under the head of Unskilled labour as Rs.9,048/ P.M.

Seeing the nature of injuries on the person of petitioner, which may took considerable time to heal up, so an amount of Rs.36,192/ ( ie Four months Minimum wages ) is awarded to the petitioner for loss of earning.

sentences.text: As per the disability certificate Ex.PW2/A, the petitioner has suffered 13% permanent disability in relation to his left lower limb.
Seeing age and occupation of petitioner, his functional disability is taken as 07% qua the whole body.

Counting in this way, his loss to future earnings comes to Rs.
1,80,887.61 (Rs. 12,667.20/x 12 x 17 x 07/100).
This amount of Rs. 1,80,887.61 ( in lump sum 1,81,000/) is allowed to petitioner, as loss of future earnings, due to permanent disability.

Loss of amenities owing to permanent disability:
20.
A person who became injured, in my opinion would have suffered a lot than a person who had lost his life in an accident.
An injured has to face lots of atrocities due to the injuries caused to him in an accident.

Herein the present case the injured has a total permanent physical disability of 13%
(Thirteen percent).

Before the accident, he was doing private job and not dependent upon any one but after the accident he was dependent upon others for his household chorus for a considerable period of time and the mental agony which victim as well as his family members had suffered is immense and the eclipse that has come in the life of victim after the accident will never go away till he lives on this earth, hence, a sum of Rs. 10,000/ is awarded to himfor loss of amenities.
Pain and suffering 21.

The next point that is to be discussed is pain and suffering and to calculate the same, the nature of injuries caused to the injured due to the accident, duration for which he got medical treatment and he was constrained to live in bed are few factors which must be taken into account.
After the accident, petitioner was firstly taken to Irena Swastik Hospital, Najafgarh,Delhi thereafter taken to Lok Nayak Hospital Delhi.

He remained admitted in hospital wef 07.10.2015 to 20.10.2015 and from MACT No. 1646/16 Arun Kumar Vs Ajay Kumar & Ors Page No. 12 of 16 27.10.2015 to 01.11.2015.There are injuries fractures of both bones of right leg with left knee and fractured of Pelvic Bone Pubic Rami.

It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his complete life, the mental agony which he faces cannot be considered.
The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination, such a scenario could shake even braver of bravest.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.
To compensate petitioner under this head, a sum of Rs.50,000/ is awarded to him.

The submission of Ld Counsel for R.3 is that the Insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
It is submitted that the offending vehicle being driven by Respondent No.1 was not possessing any valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
It is submitted that Driving license allegedly issued by RTO Faridabad upon verification was found not to have been issued from RTO Faridabad.
In this regard Respondent No.3 has examined R3W1 Sh Pulkit Sikkha.
He has proved the application for verification of D/L and D/L Verification report submitted by IO as vide Ex R3W1/1 to R3W1/3.
He has also proved the copy of notice U/O 12 rule 8 CPC vide Ex R3W1/4.
So it is proved that offending vehicle was being driven by R.1 without having valid and effective driving license at the time of accident which is violation of contract between R2 and R3.

Considering circumstances of petitioner, 25% of the amount of compensation alongwith awarded interest be released to the petitioner by way of transferring the same in his saving bank account.

It is directed that 75%
of amount alongwith awarded interest of compensation be kept in the form of FDRs ie two FDRs of equal amount in any nationalized bank ( ie petitioner's bank) in the name of petitioner for a period of one year to two years with cumulative interest.
29. The salient features as pres cribed in the judgment in Rajesh Tyagi Vs. Ramesh Chandra Gupta FAO No. 842/2009 and MAC. App. No. 422/2009 decided on 07.11.2014 are to be applied:
(i) Original fixed deposit receipt be retained by the bank in safe custody.
However, the original passbook shall be given to the claimant along with the photocopy of the FDR.
(ii) The original fixed deposit receipt be handed over to the claimant at the end of the fixed deposit period.
(iii) Photo identity card shall be issued to the claimant and the withdrawal shall be permitted only after due verification by the Bank of the identity card of the claimant.
(iv) No cheque book/ATM/debit card/credit card shall be issued to the claimant without permission of the Court.
MACT No. 1646/16 Arun Kumar Vs Ajay Kumar & Ors Page No. 15 of 16 (v) No loan, advance or withdrawal or premature encashment shall be allowed on the fixed deposit without permission of the Court.
27. Respondent no.3 is directed to deposit entire amount of compensation with this tribunal, within 30 days from today, with advance notice to petitioner.
